In detail

San Cristobal (San Cristobal de los Angeles) is one of the most extensively documented barrios in this entire research: repeated narcopiso dismantlings through 2025-2026 (including a February 2026 police clearance of an entire block used for drug plantations), press descriptions of Latin gangs and narcopisos as an 'invisible' entrenched problem since at least 2023, a car-theft wave from February 2026 onward, and residents organising street patrols due to a wave of robberies as recently as May 2026. Vozpopuli named the barrio the 'zona cero' (ground zero) of Madrid Police's anti-narcopiso operations. Sources checked: EL PAIS, 19 Feb 2026; ABC, 18 May 2023; Telemadrid, 24 Mar 2026 & 13 May 2026; gaceta.es, 14 May 2026; Vozpopuli, 28 Mar 2025.

This specific area was reviewed against credible local sources — local and national news, municipal and police-published material, and official surveys where they exist — and the signals were consolidated across sources rather than taken from any single report, with the reasoning and the sources shown above. Madrid publishes no comparable neighbourhood-level crime dataset; where a city does publish one, Wandroz uses it instead of an assessment. Where a review finds nothing documented, that is recorded as no findings rather than as a safety rating.

Frequently asked questions

Is San Cristóbal safe?

Wandroz currently rates San Cristóbal in Madrid as an area where the data suggests extra caution relative to other neighbourhoods in Madrid, both by day and after dark. This comes from a structured local-source assessment: an area-level review of credible local sources — local and national news, municipal and police-published material, and official surveys where they exist — consolidated across sources rather than taken from a single report. Madrid publishes no comparable neighbourhood-level crime dataset; where a city does, Wandroz uses it instead.

Is San Cristóbal safe at night?

At night, San Cristóbal is rated as an area where the data suggests extra caution relative to other neighbourhoods in Madrid. If you're unsure, it's worth checking recent local reviews for your specific street or block, since a neighbourhood-wide rating can't capture block-by-block variation.

Is San Cristóbal a good area to stay in as a tourist?

San Cristóbal's day rating (an area where the data suggests extra caution relative to other neighbourhoods in Madrid) is the more relevant one for typical daytime tourist activity; check the night rating too if you'll be out late. The Booking.com link on this page searches San Cristóbal itself.

Is there official crime data for San Cristóbal?

Not an official government crime feed — San Cristóbal's rating comes from Wandroz's own current local/national press and survey research for this specific area instead (see the note on this page for what was checked and the sources used). An absence of recent negative coverage is treated as inconclusive, not as proof the area is safe. If you live in or know San Cristóbal well, you can suggest a correction using the link below.
